top3.headline: Apple ships an official Xcode plugin for Claude Code
top3.whyItMatters: iOS teams can now let agents build, test and preview apps without custom tooling.

top3.headline: Microsoft's AI Frontiers lab ends under scaling-first MAI
top3.whyItMatters: Microsoft's AI strategy now centers on scale, not research; watch where its agent talent lands.

top3.headline: Approved Claude Code commands exposed secrets in 1,122 GitHub files
top3.whyItMatters: Agent config files now carry credentials, so add them to secret scanning today.

items.title: A prompt that makes coding agents justify every file they open
items.takeaway: The agent lists the files it needs and why, waits for approval, then makes the smallest change.
items.soWhat: Gating what an agent reads may cut token spend, though no savings were measured.

items.title: Claude Code approvals leak passwords in 1,122 public GitHub files
items.takeaway: Apiiro says 'Don't Ask Again' commands with inline secrets were committed in settings files; Anthropic says it is looking into prevention.
items.soWhat: Agent settings files are now a secrets risk, so scan and gitignore them.

items.title: Theo pauses t3os and recommends Omarchy for remote agents
items.takeaway: Theo says Omarchy already has almost all the agent capabilities he wanted; he posted no benchmark numbers.
items.soWhat: One prominent builder says existing setups already cover most remote-agent needs.

items.title: Microsoft Research's AI Frontiers group ends after MAI reorg
items.takeaway: John Langford says the roughly 50-person group behind Autogen and Fara is over, and its founding leaders have left.
items.soWhat: Microsoft's AI push now favors scaling over research, and senior agent researchers are leaving.

image.alt: John Langford, hunch.net: Microsoft Research's AI Frontiers group ends after MAI reorg

items.title: Apple's Xcode plugin joins Claude Code's official marketplace
items.takeaway: Apple-authored plugin exposes Xcode via MCP: build, run and test schemes, SwiftUI previews, simulators and build logs.
items.soWhat: Native Apple development is now a first-party target for coding agents.

voices.quote: The core philosophy there is scaling, and aggressively not research.
Historically Claude Code has not done secret scrubbing (there are many good tools for that), but we are looking into what we can do to prevent this.
It's a really good choice for remote agents, and you should probably use it.
AI agents tend to over-read because more context feels safer for them.
